title: Base Ref, Cleanup, and the /batch Path

questions.prompt: An agent in a worktree fixes a bug, but the fix assumes code you committed to your feature branch this morning and haven't pushed. The agent never saw that change. What was almost certainly true?
options: `worktree.baseRef` was `"head"`, so it should have seen your commit
`worktree.baseRef` was left at the default, so the worktree branched from the remote default branch
The worktree copied tracked files but not your commit messages
The agent's model had a smaller context window than your session
questions.explanation: The default base is `"fresh"`, which branches from the repository's default branch on the remote — so unpushed work on your feature branch isn't there. Setting `"head"` is the fix. Option A is backwards. Option C confuses a checkout with commit history. Option D is a context-window issue and would show up as truncated results, not a stale tree.

questions.prompt: A worktree Claude created for a background agent is days old. You want it gone, but `git worktree remove` refuses. Why might the sweep not have taken it already?
options: The sweep only removes worktrees created by `git worktree add`
It still holds unpushed commits or changed files, which the sweep keeps on purpose
The sweep runs only at session startup and you haven't restarted
Claude-created worktrees can never be swept, only removed by hand
questions.explanation: The sweep deliberately skips any worktree that still holds work — changed or untracked files, or unpushed commits — so a worktree with real work stays until you deal with it, often locked while an agent runs. The sweep targets Claude-created worktrees (those with a marker), not `git worktree add` ones, which it keeps. It isn't a startup-only job, and Claude-created worktrees are exactly what it removes when they're clean and old.

questions.prompt: A colleague asks you to change one function signature in one file. They suggest `/batch`. What should you tell them?
options: Yes — `/batch` runs one worktree per unit, so one unit is fine
No — `/batch` decomposes a large change into 5 to 30 units; a one-file change doesn't need fan-out
No — `/batch` needs a `WorktreeCreate` hook even in a git repo
Yes — `/batch` is required any time more than one file changes
questions.explanation: `/batch` is built for large-scale changes it can split into 5–30 independent units; a single-file edit gains nothing and pays coordination overhead. It works in a git repository without a hook — the hook is for non-git version control. Nothing requires `/batch` merely because more than one file changes.

questions.prompt: You set `worktree.baseRef` to `feature-x`, the name of your branch, and start a worktree. It fails. What is the correct fix?
options: Quote the branch name so the shell doesn't expand it
Use `"head"` while checked out on that branch, or create the worktree with `git worktree add`
Set `baseRef` to the branch's commit hash instead
questions.explanation: `baseRef` accepts only `"fresh"` or `"head"` — it can't name a branch, so the correct move is `"head"` from that branch or a manual `git worktree add`. Quoting or a commit hash doesn't change the accepted values. The agent-teams variable is unrelated to worktree creation.
